# FoodAllo

> Public-interest open concept for fair food and essentials allocation when markets fail. Complements aid and stockpiles — does not replace them. Open concept; professional implementation available.

Canonical site: https://foodallo.github.io/foodallo-open-concept/  
Contact: assistant@foodallo.com  
Status (2026-10-05): Public open concept and rule walkthrough. No live nationwide distribution service claimed. License: MIT for documentation in the GitHub repository.

## What FoodAllo is

FoodAllo documents a need-based allocation layer for food and life-essential non-food in shortage: published rules (vulnerable-first, household caps), multi-channel access including without a smartphone. It answers who gets what when — beside stockpiles (what/where) and crisis law (authority / orderly issue, e.g. Germany’s ESVG).

Initiated by David Wieland, a practitioner with about 20 years of experience in the fire service and in disaster and civil protection. Developed by the FoodAllo project team. Source: https://foodallo.github.io/foodallo-open-concept/#about

## What FoodAllo is not

- Not a claim to end all hunger or produce food
- Not a replacement for humanitarian aid, stockpiles, or legal preparedness (e.g. ESVG)
- Not surveillance consumer profiling
- Not a live nationwide government system
- Not vendor lock-in: the concept is openly documented

- [Open allocation walkthrough — market disrupted](https://foodallo.github.io/foodallo-open-concept/demo.html?preset=markt): No account. Compare first-come vs shares by need.
- [Shortage week walkthrough](https://foodallo.github.io/foodallo-open-concept/demo.html): Same rules without an account.
- [No smartphone / analog channel](https://foodallo.github.io/foodallo-open-concept/analog.html): Desk, neighbour/proxy, paper code — same max share.
- [Elimination engine](https://foodallo.github.io/foodallo-open-concept/eliminationsmaschine.html): Transparent rule walkthrough.
- [For crisis responders](https://foodallo.github.io/foodallo-open-concept/for-responders.html): How FoodAllo complements aid and stockpiles as an allocation layer.
- [For public authorities](https://foodallo.github.io/foodallo-open-concept/for-authorities.html): How FoodAllo complements stockpiles and crisis law as an allocation layer. Open concept, professional implementation.
- [For organisations](https://foodallo.github.io/foodallo-open-concept/#organisations): Pilot support, implementation, training and operation for municipalities, authorities and relief organisations.
